newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop soymeal down, soyoil hits 4-year low.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop soymeal down, soyoil hits 4-year low.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures were sharply lower and the December briefly dropped the $10.00 per ton daily limit, keying off of bearish USDA acreage data.
Soyoil set contract lows across the board and the July hit the lowest level for a spot month since 1993.
USDA on Monday pegged 1997 U.S. soybean acreage at 70.85 million acres, the highest since 1982 and above trade expectations for 68.4 million.
Floor sources reported broad-based selling in soymeal but said orders were mostly small. "There were a lot of small-lot orders for 20 to 30 lots but no big orders," a trader said.
At 1006 CDT, soymeal was down $9.10 to $3.70 per ton with December off $9.10 at $201.50. Soyoil was down 0.84 to 0.66 cent per lb with December down 0.84 at 21.95.
The July soyoil contract traded at 21.45 cents, a contract low and the lowest for a nearby month since June 1993.
